speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what programmes are in place to support companies in making work and the work environment age-friendly to enable companies to leverage the competencies of their older employees and for older workers to do their best work; (b) what is the progress of companies establishing and adopting more age-friendly work practices; and (c) what is the progress of companies retraining their older workers to enable them to take on new opportunities within the organisation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Even without the grants, many progressive companies have implemented age-friendly practices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: These age-friendly measures include job redesign, flexible work arrangements (FDWs) and well-being programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The Government continues to support our seniors to upgrade their skills alongside the changing needs of the industry.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For example, the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy provides higher funding support for eligible Singaporeans aged 40 and over.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This could be up to 90% of course fees for SkillsFuture Singapore supported courses and at least 90% of programme costs for MOE-subsidised courses in our institutes of higher learning.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This move will extend the age ceiling of more jobs and workers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Older workers are more likely to look to employers to indicate the kind of training they should undertake.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Could I just ask how has this helped in terms of making it easier for employers to offer opportunities for re-employment of their employees who have reached retirement age?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: As well as what has been the feedback from older workers, in terms of this helping in their re-employment and hearing that it is still task-oriented, but has it helped in their re-employment opportunities with the employers?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I wish to thank the Member Ms Jessica Tan for her supplementary questions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure her that the Government is always looking at ways to help workers who wish to work longer to let them enjoy productive longevity.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: At the same time, we stand ready to support the companies to make their work and also work environment age-friendly in support of hiring older workers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In the last few years, we have put in place many things, not just the policies but also measures, programmes and schemes and even tripartite guidelines, and now, the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers' 22 recommendations to allow older workers to work as long as they are willing to work and are able to work and to equip the employers to make the workplace more age-friendly.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Some of the workers may choose not to work after a certain age and some of them may choose to vary their intensity, maybe they want FWAs, part-time and so on.
